maria: Heads-up — saw a nasty perf regression in the runtime autotuner this morning. For several causal SDPA workloads with small head_dim (16, 24) the tuner is picking a v1 fallback that is ~2x slower than the v3 path we used to prefer. Repro script attached: `./ci/run_flash_perf.sh --model=tiny-llm --head-dim=24 --seq=512 --batch=4`

jonathan: Can you paste the autotune/profiler log? also which GPU (A10/3090/4090)?

maria: Running on g4dn (A10G) and gpus in staging (4090). Here's the snippet from the kernel decision log: 
```
[autotune] model=tiny-llm head_dim=24 seq_len=512 batch=4 hw=A10G
candidate: flashattn_v3_causal -> estimated_throughput=230k tok/s cost_align=high compat=false (head_dim % 32 != 0)
candidate: flashattn_v1_causal -> estimated_throughput=120k tok/s cost_align=low compat=true -> SELECTED
reason: compat_flag trumps throughput estimate
```

kevin: hmm. That compat flag is ancient — it was added when v3 used a fused-warp layout that required 32-alignment for good SMEM usage. But we added a slower per-warp fallback in v3 last quarter that should handle 16/24 at a lower perf hit, and the tuner is not aware of that fallback. Did the perf model not pick up the fallback numbers?

sasha: Also worth noting: v3's small-head fallback exposes a different KV cache layout. For causal runs with caching enabled we see an extra memcpy to align KV which increases overhead at small batch sizes and flips the economics. I saw this in a trace: 
```
TRACE: kvcache: write_alignment_copy 1.6ms per step when head_dim=24 batch=4
TRACE: v3_fallback_extra_copy 0.9ms
```
That combined with shorter seqs (<=512) makes the theoretical v3 advantage smaller in practice.

perf-bot: perf/regression check summary (staging):
- tiny-llm head_dim=24 seq=512 batch=4: v1 selected, 118k tok/s
- tiny-llm head_dim=24 seq=512 batch=4 (force v3): 225k tok/s raw kernel, but end-to-end 135k tok/s due to KV memcpy and extra kernel launches
- delta: +17% end-to-end when forcing v3 vs autotuned v1 (surprising given log)

jonathan: So raw kernel throughput favors v3 but runtime bookkeeping (KV layout + extra kernel calls) erodes benefit. Two levers: 1) change autotuner scoring to use measured end-to-end estimates (kernel + KV costs) instead of kernel-only; 2) add cheap padding to head_dim at allocation time (pad to 32) so v3 stays fully efficient. Padding tradeoffs: extra memory + cache pressure.

kevin: Agreed. I ran microbenchmarks this morning and here are the numbers: 
`head_dim=16` 
- v3_raw: 210k tok/s, end2end: 140k (kv overhead 35%)
- v1_raw: 105k tok/s, end2end: 105k
`head_dim=24` similar pattern. So a padding-to-32 option yields v3 end2end ~210k but increases mem by 33% for KV buffers. For many customers padding is fine.

maria: Proposed immediate mitigation: autotuner change to prefer v3 if predicted end2end > 1.2x v1 (config flag) and add an experimental runtime option `runtime.kv.pad_head_dim=32` that can be enabled per-tenant. I'll open a tiny canary PR.

kevin: For the autotuner, we should incorporate a simple model: perf_score = kernel_est / (1 + kv_overhead_est). We can heuristically estimate kv_overhead_est as a function of head_dim and batch size from the microbench table. I'll sketch a patch. Also add an A/B rollout for dedicated customers.

sasha: Another idea: make the v3 fallback set a special nvshmem-friendly layout that avoids the memcpy on cache writes. That might be more invasive but would preserve memory efficiency without padding. Could be medium-term.

maria: Patch opened: `r/1234` — autotune.prefer_v3_ratio default=1.2, autotune.kv_overhead_table contains small-head entries. Also added a CLI toggle: `--runtime-kv-pad=32`. Please try canary on staging and run nightly perf job `perf/nightly/eng-runtime/flashattn-heads`

kevin: Running canary now on staging (A10G pool). Will post perf-bot summary in ~30m.

perf-bot: Canary run kickoff: job=flashattn-heads canary_id=autotune-v3-2026-03-17

jonathan: FYI, let's add a unit test that forces head_dim padding path and validates that cache offsets are stable (no off-by-one) — that caught us last time.

maria: Good call. adding unit test in PR.

kevin: If canary looks good, we should land the autotuner change behind a feature flag and enable for 10% of hosters first. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks all — appreciate the quick triage. I'll follow up with logs and the PR link in this thread. :shipit:
